newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Winter demand props up jet.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Winter demand props up jet.

text.p: Jet fuel swaps was firm late Thursday afternoon as more demand emerged from North Asia for the winter heating fuel, industry sources said.
This week South Korea bought a February jet/kerosene cargo at a premium of about $2.40 over Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis, up about 40 cents from previous deal.
Demand was also seen from China which bought a jet fuel cargo for January arrival at around $2.00 premium to Singapore spot quotes, on a c-and-f basis.
The January jet/gas oil spread or regrade was last quoted at $1.35/$1.50, about 10 cents up from Wednesday.

Gas oil swaps extended its midday hike with January traded this afternoon at $31.20 and $31.24 a barrel. January gas oil swaps traded in the morning at $32.00, $32.10 and $32.15 a barrel, up from Wednesday's $31.90/$32.00, brokers said.
The market was last quoted at $32.20/$32.35, they said.
Traders said the market is also bullish due to expectations of Chinese buying for until end January delivery cargoes and firmer crude values.
January naphtha was indicated firmer in quiet trade at $24.10/$24.30 per barrel.
Fuel oil was unchanged despite higher physical trade on Wednesday when a 20,000-tonne cargo was traded at $124.00 per tonne. January swaps was last quoted at $120.50/$121.75 per tonne.
